topics.topic: {'title': "Why do you feel 'guilty' when you are not busy?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Productivity Dysmorphia & Internalized Protestant Work Ethic', 'angle': "Analyzing the common Vietnamese 'hustle culture' where young professionals feel a sense of failure or anxiety during weekends or holidays if they aren't 'doing something productive,' leading to chronic burnout even during rest."}

{'title': "Why do you 'over-apologize' to your boss even when you did nothing wrong?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Appeasement Reflex & Conflict Avoidance Bias', 'angle': "Analyzing the common Vietnamese workplace culture where employees reflexively say 'Em xin lỗi' to avoid perceived confrontation or authority-based anxiety, even when the mistake belongs to the company or the manager, leading to a loss of professional self-worth."}

{'title': "Why do you 'doom-scroll' at 2 AM despite being exhausted?", 'psychological_effect': 'Revenge Bedtime Procrastination & Cognitive Offloading', 'angle': "Analyzing the Vietnamese urban phenomenon where young people, feeling they have no control over their long, draining workdays, 'steal' back time at night by scrolling endlessly, essentially sacrificing their sleep to reclaim a sense of personal autonomy."}

{'title': "Why do you feel a strange urge to 'buy' your parents' love with expensive gifts while living far away?", 'psychological_effect': 'The Guilt-Induced Compensatory Altruism & Emotional Outsourcing', 'angle': "Analyzing the common Vietnamese 'expat' or urban-migrant phenomenon where children working in big cities feel immense pressure to send money or luxury goods back home to 'buy' peace of mind, essentially using material gifts as a substitute for the physical presence and emotional labor they cannot provide due to their busy careers."}
